title: Shakshuka
subtitle: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce
excerpt: A simple, deeply satisfying one-pan breakfast of eggs cooked directly in a spiced tomato sauce. On the table in 30 minutes and made from mostly pantry ingredients.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from classic Middle Eastern and North African shakshuka preparations.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated. Reheat to a simmer, then crack in the eggs and proceed.

content.text: Shakshuka is eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce. The dish is North African and Middle Eastern in origin; the name translates roughly as a mixture. The spicing varies by region and household. This version uses the classic base of onion, pepper, tomato, and cumin. A deep frying pan with a lid is essential: the eggs cook from below via the sauce and from above via trapped steam.

Build the base. Heat the olive oil in a wide, deep frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and beginning to turn golden at the edges. Add the red pepper and cook for another 5 minutes until softened.

Add the aromatics. Add the garlic and chilli, reduce the heat slightly and cook for 2 minutes. Add the cumin, sweet paprika, smoked paprika and coriander-ground. Stir for 1 minute to coat everything in the spices and cook off any raw flour taste.

Add the tomatoes. Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the tinned tomatoes, season generously with salt and black pepper. Crush the tomatoes with the back of a spoon if whole. Bring to the boil, then simmer over medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the oil is beginning to pool at the edges. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Add the eggs. Use the back of a spoon to create 8 wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each well. Try not to break the yolks.

Cover and cook the eggs. Cover the pan tightly with a lid. Cook over medium-low heat for 5 to 7 minutes for eggs with set whites and runny yolks, or 8 to 10 minutes for fully set yolks. Check at 5 minutes: the whites should be completely opaque but the yolks should still wobble when you shake the pan gently.
Serve straight from the pan. Scatter over the fresh coriander and crumbled feta if using. Bring the pan to the table and serve with warm flatbread or toasted sourdough to scoop up the sauce.

items.symptom: Egg whites are still runny after the stated time
items.cause: The sauce was not hot enough before the eggs were added, or the lid did not seal well.
items.fix: Make sure the sauce is at a gentle simmer before adding the eggs. Check the lid seals properly: if steam is escaping, the eggs will not cook evenly. Add another 2 minutes.

items.symptom: Yolks are fully set before the whites have cooked through
items.fix: Keep the heat at medium-low. The eggs cook gently via steam rather than direct heat from below.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thin and watery
items.cause: The tinned tomatoes were not reduced enough before adding the eggs.
items.fix: Remove the eggs (or cover and set aside briefly if already in). Return the sauce to a high heat and boil until thickened. Return the eggs and finish as above.

items.cause: The onion and pepper were not cooked long enough, or too much tinned tomato without enough balance.
items.fix: Add a pinch of sugar and a little more olive oil to the sauce. Stir and taste. A longer initial cook on the onion prevents bitterness from developing in the first place.
